verdicts.reason: Output 1 caught that current spend runs over the monthly budget, gave per-ad-set daily budgets and a hard cap; Output 2 is solid but misses the over-budget point.

Output 1 concentrates test spend ($350 per ad group) and uses three-read day-30 verdict with a blended check; Output 2 spreads $100 per ad group, too thin to learn, and judges on UTM-only count that under-reports TikTok.
Output 2 has sharper hooks, headlines, safe zones and concrete test rules; Output 1 concepts are more visually distinct but its test guidance is thinner.

Output 1 has spoken plus on-screen disclosure in the video, rights and deliverables in the creator brief, and a stronger blind-test idea; Output 2 relies on toggles and a backup disclosure and uses UK spelling for a US brand.
Both verified limits; Output 1 adds the brand-name angle, FSSAI check and a clear keep/cut rule with replacement copy.
Output 2 leads with the top review theme in stronger bullets and avoids visible [X] placeholders in the live copy while still repeating the cash limit at every decision point.

Output 2 front-loads the first week, has subject variants, unique codes, checkout-skip logic and an interactive WhatsApp with sample values; Output 1 is good but longer and its WhatsApp is just a reminder.
Output 2 derives the lapse line from the data, keeps offers to message 3 and protects margin, adds a fix-first group, and gives a range with a decision rule; Output 1's lifts are more optimistic.

Output 1 puts every move in the same unit (share of revenue), correctly sizes contribution margin falling about 45%, and gives targets for each scorecard metric; Output 2 mixes per-1,000 units so moves are hard to rank.
Both arithmetic checks hold; Output 1 adds a cautious and bad case with break-even, a sample-size calculation and a dated, stop-ruled test plan.
Output 2 ranks the trial line higher, uses delivered orders for the COD guardrail, sizes every test on the order metric and covers return settlement; Output 1 rests three tests on add-to-cart.

Output 2 has sample values and headers for submission, a failed-delivery template, agent capacity math, a cart holdout, a justified Rs 20 prepaid offer and call scripts; Output 1 lacks submission samples and the missed-delivery step.
